articles.title: With $720M round, Britain’s Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips
articles.snippet: Fractile has now become one of the top-funded players in the race for purpose-built AI chips.
articles.text:
Fractile , a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund with hopes of “ensuring the U.K. has a greater stake in the hardware that will underpin its future economy,” its government stated .
Alongside the likes of Axelera , Etched , and OLIX , this makes Fractile one of the top-funded startup players in the race for purpose-built AI chips. Such chips are one of several avenues being explored to reduce the cost of inference — aka using increasingly demanding AI models in production.
However, Fractile seeks to go beyond hardware with a full-stack approach that also includes a machine learning compiler to maximize the speed at which LLMs will get executed on its chips.
As a result, the company frames itself as a frontier AI company, and its latest round led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Redpoint was priced accordingly. According to the British government, the valuation was “over £5 billion” — quite possibly $7 billion, a figure reported both by the Financial Times and a Reuters source .
Still, Fractile’s main differentiator will arguably be its hardware design. After a pivot , its approach now revolves on DRAM, the most common type of RAM, but stacked on top of each chip in such a way that it is hoping will bypass the usual tradeoff between memory and capacity.
This tradeoff has become more problematic with the rise of agentic AI, as companies seek to perform longer chains of tasks with large models without compromising on speed. As compute struggles to keep up, hopes are high for AI chips, despite their limited availability to date.
In a LinkedIn post , Fractile CEO Walter Goodwin wrote that “there is still a lot of work ahead” for the company, and that the new funding will enable the startup to “ship [its] first chips and systems next year.”

articles.title: Edgevana: $700 Million AI Infrastructure Agreements Bring Committed Demand To $7 Billion
articles.snippet:
Edgevana, an AI computing infrastructure company, has secured more than $700 million in fully committed, multiyear agreements to deploy NVIDIA Blackwell computing systems across North America and Europe. The contracts expand the company's committed customer demand to approximately $7 billion, with an additional active business pipeline exceeding $20 billion.
The post Edgevana: $700 Million AI Infrastructure Agreements Bring Committed Demand To $7 Billion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Edgevana: $700 Million AI Infrastructure Agreements Bring Committed Demand To $7 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 3:26 PM
Edgevana: $700 Million AI Infrastructure Agreements Bring Committed Demand To $7 Billion
Edgevana, an AI computing infrastructure company, has secured more than $700 million in fully committed, multiyear agreements to deploy NVIDIA Blackwell computing systems across North America and Europe. The contracts expand the company’s committed customer demand to approximately $7 billion, with an additional active business pipeline exceeding $20 billion.
The agreements involve take-or-pay commitments under which customers contract for computing capacity over multiple years.
Edgevana intends to deploy NVIDIA B300 GPUs and GB300 systems through its distributed data center infrastructure.
The company is developing a model that combines existing power availability, data center facilities, computing equipment, and high-speed network connectivity.
By coordinating these resources across multiple locations, Edgevana aims to accelerate the delivery of production-ready AI computing capacity.
The company says its approach can bring tens of megawatts of high-density AI infrastructure online within approximately 90 to 120 days.
Traditional data center development projects can require substantially longer timelines because of challenges involving land acquisition, utility connections, power infrastructure, equipment procurement, and construction.
Edgevana’s strategy centers on identifying locations where power and other essential infrastructure are already available.
The company then coordinates deployment of computing systems across its network, creating what it describes as a virtual campus.
This approach allows customers to access distributed infrastructure through a unified management environment.
Edgevana believes the model is particularly relevant as AI workloads shift from centralized model training toward inference applications supporting active users and business systems.
Inference workloads can require low latency, reliable network connectivity, and geographically distributed computing resources.
These requirements create opportunities for infrastructure providers capable of deploying AI compute closer to end users.
Edgevana’s experience includes providing low-latency infrastructure for high-frequency trading and supporting edge computing operations for two major hyperscale technology companies.
The company is applying those capabilities to the deployment of advanced AI accelerators.
Its global infrastructure network includes 17 operational data center locations, with another 10 sites under active development.
According to Edgevana, platforms supported by its infrastructure serve more than 10,000 downstream enterprise customers.
The company’s business model combines long-term energy supply arrangements, access to GPU computing equipment, and committed customer contracts.
By securing customer demand before deployment, Edgevana seeks to reduce financial exposure and improve capital efficiency.
The approach is also intended to help customers avoid delays associated with constructing entirely new data centers.
Edgevana believes pre-energized infrastructure can provide a competitive advantage as demand for high-performance AI computing increases.
Power availability has become an important constraint in the development of large AI data centers.

articles.title: Peloton: $700 Million Senior Secured Notes Offering Upsized From $600 Million As Part Of Debt Refinancing
articles.snippet:
Peloton Interactive has announced the pricing of an upsized $700 million senior secured notes offering carrying an annual interest rate of 8.625% and maturing in 2032. The offering, increased from an originally announced $600 million, is part of a broader refinancing initiative that also includes a proposed $200 million revolving credit facility.
The post Peloton: $700 Million Senior Secured Notes Offering Upsized From $600 Million As Part Of Debt Refinancing appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Peloton: $700 Million Senior Secured Notes Offering Upsized From $600 Million As Part Of Debt Refinancing
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:20 AM
Peloton: $700 Million Senior Secured Notes Offering Upsized From $600 Million As Part Of Debt Refinancing
Peloton Interactive has announced the pricing of an upsized $700 million senior secured notes offering carrying an annual interest rate of 8.625% and maturing in 2032. The offering, increased from an originally announced $600 million, is part of a broader refinancing initiative that also includes a proposed $200 million revolving credit facility.
The New York-based connected fitness company expects the notes offering to generate approximately $700 million in gross proceeds before underwriting discounts, commissions, and other transaction expenses.
The transaction is expected to settle on November 20, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.
Peloton intends to use the net proceeds, together with existing cash, to repay all outstanding borrowings under its current $1 billion five-year term loan facility.
The existing term loan agreement will be terminated following repayment.
The refinancing is designed to restructure Peloton’s debt obligations by replacing its outstanding term loans with senior secured notes carrying a maturity date in 2032.
The notes will represent senior secured obligations of the company, meaning they will benefit from specified collateral arrangements and rank according to the terms established in the financing documents.
The annual interest rate of 8.625% determines the stated interest expense associated with the notes.
At the full $700 million principal amount, the stated annual interest obligation would total approximately $60.4 million before considering any applicable adjustments or other financing costs.
The refinancing also includes Peloton’s proposed entry into a new $200 million revolving credit facility with a five-year term.
A revolving credit facility allows a company to borrow, repay, and potentially borrow again within an established credit limit, subject to the agreement’s terms.
Such facilities can provide financial flexibility for working capital needs, operating expenses, and other corporate requirements.
Peloton’s proposed revolving facility would complement its longer-term debt financing by providing an additional source of potential liquidity.
However, the company emphasized that completion of the senior secured notes offering is not dependent on entering into the new revolving credit facility.
The notes offering is also not conditioned on repayment of the existing term loan facility.
These provisions allow the offering to close independently of the other components of the broader refinancing initiative.
Expanded Offering And Use Of Proceeds
Peloton increased the offering from $600 million to $700 million, representing an additional $100 million in planned debt issuance.
The expansion provides additional proceeds that can be applied toward the company’s refinancing requirements.
Peloton plans to combine the proceeds with cash on hand to repay the remaining loans outstanding under its existing term loan facility and cover associated transaction expenses.
The announced $1 billion figure refers to the size of the existing facility rather than a confirmed amount currently outstanding.
Consequently, the company has not specified the precise cash contribution required to complete the repayment.

articles.title: Uforce Raises $700M in Series A Funding to Expand Ukraine-Focused Autonomous Defense Production
articles.snippet: Uforce Raises $700M in Series A Funding to Expand Ukraine-Focused Autonomous Defense Production AI Insider
articles.text:
Physical AI · Defence & Autonomous Systems
Uforce Raises $700M in Series A Funding to Expand Ukraine-Focused Autonomous Defense Production
By Greg Bock · 13 November 2026 · 3 min read
Credit: Uforce
Insider Brief
Ukraine-founded defense technology company Uforce raised $700 million in Series A funding at a $6 billion valuation to expand production of autonomous military systems for Ukraine and allied nations.
The round was co-led by Valor Equity Partners and the UK National Wealth Fund, with participation from the U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund and investors including Menlo Ventures, Xantium and Hiro Capital.
Uforce plans to expand manufacturing of its MAGURA maritime drones, NEMESIS aerial drones, LIUT ground vehicles and PREDATOR turret systems across allied countries, while supporting operations and research in Ukraine.
Ukraine-founded defense technology company Uforce has raised $700 million in Series A funding at a $6 billion valuation to expand production of autonomous military systems for Ukraine and allied nations.
The round was co-led by Valor Equity Partners and the UK National Wealth Fund, with participation from the U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund, according to Uforce . Other investors included Menlo Ventures , Xantium and Hiro Capital, while existing backers Shield Capital , Ballistic Ventures , Lakestar and Squadra increased their stakes.
Headquartered in London, with major operations in Kyiv and Washington, Uforce develops uncrewed systems for air, land and sea operations, along with AI software for coordinating and controlling them. The company said the funding will support manufacturing expansion across the United States, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, while maintaining production and supplies for Ukrainian forces despite continued attacks in Ukraine.
Expanding Autonomous Defense Production
Uforce plans to increase production and research and development across four product families: MAGURA uncrewed surface vessels, NEMESIS aerial drones, LIUT ground vehicles and PREDATOR turret systems.
The company also anticipates working with partners in allied countries to adapt existing maritime and automotive manufacturing facilities for defense production.
Uforce recently announced a partnership with ReconCraft to expand U.S. manufacturing of its Maritime Autonomous Guard Unmanned Robotic Apparatus (MAGURA) vessels. It also plans to build on relationships within NATO and Joint Expeditionary Force networks and continue participating as a founding member of the EU-Ukraine Drone Alliance.
CEO Oleg Rogynskyy said the financing will help increase production for Ukraine while providing allied nations with autonomous systems they can deploy, integrate and maintain.
“The war in Ukraine has shown that in an increasingly volatile world, effective defense requires systems that can keep improving as threats change,” noted Rogynskyy. “Governments and the technology ecosystem need to come together to develop cost-effective, interoperable, and autonomous platforms that are ready to fight now, and can evolve to meet future needs.”
Investment Supports Ukrainian Operations
The U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund’s participation will specifically support Uforce’s operations in Ukraine, including staffing, research and development, and new products. The fund was established jointly by the United States and Ukraine to attract investment into reconstruction, economic development and strategic industries.

articles.title: African tech startups raised $684M in first nine months of 2026, led by Nairobi with $277M following Spiro’s $215M Series E
articles.snippet: African tech startups raised $684M in first nine months of 2026, led by Nairobi with $277M following Spiro’s $215M Series E fundsforNGOs News
articles.text:
African tech startups raised $684M in first nine months of 2026, led by Nairobi with $277M following Spiro’s $215M Series E
Dated: November 9, 2026
African tech companies raised $684 million in the first nine months of 2026, according to a Tracxn Technologies report cited by AU-Startups, representing a 30% year-on-year increase from $527 million in the same period of 2025. The total was deployed across 100 funding rounds, slightly fewer than the 103 rounds recorded the year before.
The report found that Nairobi led African startup fundraising, attracting $277 million—about 41% of the continent-wide total for the period. The concentration is largely linked to a single transaction: Spiro’s $215 million Series E round in Nairobi, which followed the company’s broader $270 million funding round completed in June 2026.
Funding growth alongside fewer deals
While overall capital increased, the number of rounds fell by 3% year on year, signaling a more selective environment for investors. The report describes a trend in which capital is increasingly directed toward larger transactions and businesses demonstrating clear commercial potential, rather than earlier-stage ventures.
For early-stage founders—particularly those at pre-seed and seed—this environment can make fundraising more challenging, the report suggests, as investors focus on later-stage traction and scale-ready models.
Spiro’s Series E and the shift toward infrastructure-style cleantech
Spiro, an electric vehicle and battery-swapping company, finalized its $270 million funding round in June 2026, with $215 million of that amount coming as equity financing. The Series E included participation from institutional investors Impact Fund Denmark and Equitane, according to the report.
The company operates across seven African countries, including Kenya, Rwanda and Nigeria. Spiro says it has deployed more than 100,000 electric vehicles and established over 2,500 battery-swapping stations on the continent, framing the investment as support for scaling electric mobility infrastructure.
The funding also reflects a broader pattern described by the report: greater attention to asset-heavy, infrastructure-style businesses in mobility and clean energy. It notes that this emphasis contrasts with earlier funding cycles that often favored software-only models, and it highlights an increased use of debt and blended finance alongside equity.
Nairobi’s dominance and other emerging hubs
Nairobi’s $277 million share in the first nine months of 2026 rose sharply from $61 million in the same period of 2025, with the increase attributed almost entirely to Spiro’s $270 million contribution to the city’s total. Other hubs cited include Cairo, which raised $126 million, and Abuja, which attracted $52 million.
In Abuja, the report states that the funding was driven entirely by Terra across three seed rounds. The geographic concentration matters because it suggests that growth in headline capital does not automatically translate into evenly distributed investment opportunities across Africa’s ecosystems.
The article also notes discrepancies between data providers: Tracxn reported $684 million, while other analyses pointed to higher totals—TechCabal Insights estimated $2.49 billion across 315 deals, and Condia reported about $2.45 billion in disclosed funding for the same period. The differences are attributed to varying inclusion criteria across trackers.

Twelve Secures $645 Million to Revolutionize Sustainable Aviation Fuel
Twelve raised $645 million, led by TPG Rise Climate, to scale technology that turns captured CO2, water, and renewable energy into E-Jet sustainable aviation fuel. The round funds AirPlant One in Moses Lake, Washington.
Written by Causeartist
Tagged
Carbon Climate Tech Climate Change Funding Round Sustainable Aviation
Last updated: November 13, 2026
Photo credit: Causeartist
Featured companies
Twelve A world made from air.
Key takeaways
Twelve announced a $645 million funding round led by TPG Rise Climate to scale carbon-to-fuel technology.
The financing combines $400 million in project equity from TPG Rise Climate, about $200 million in Series C funding, and $45 million in credit facilities.
Series C was co-led by Capricorn Investment Group and Pulse Fund, with DCVC, Munich Re Ventures, and Emerson Collective participating.
AirPlant One, Twelve's sustainable aviation fuel facility in Moses Lake, Washington, was scheduled to start operations in 2025 and produce E-Jet fuel from biogenic CO2, water, and renewable energy.
Twelve says the fuel is projected to cut lifecycle emissions by up to 90% versus conventional fossil jet fuel, with future plants supplying Alaska Airlines and International Airlines Group.
Twelve, an innovative carbon transformation company, has announced a $645 million funding round led by TPG Rise Climate.
This funding is set to propel Twelve's mission of converting captured carbon dioxide into valuable chemicals, fuels, and essential products traditionally derived from fossil fuels.
The financing includes a strategic blend of $400 million in project equity from TPG Rise Climate , $200 million in Series C financing, and an additional $45 million in credit facilities from prominent renewable energy sector funders, marking it as one of the largest rounds in the e-fuels industry to date.
About Twelve
Twelve is a leader in carbon transformation technology, dedicated to eliminating global emissions and forging a fossil-free future.
Through their Opus™ Carbon Transformation System , Twelve converts CO2, water, and renewable energy into essential hydrocarbons used in chemicals, materials, and fuels, displacing the need for fossil fuels across industrial and everyday product supply chains.

New investors include the US–Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund (URIF), Menlo Ventures, Xantium and Hiro Capital. Existing backers Shield Capital, Ballistic Ventures, Lakestar and Squadra increased their stakes.
Worker.ai , a company operating system for small businesses backed by Veeam founder Ratmir Timashev, has acquired DeltaGen , a Prague-based startup that builds real-time voice AI. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. All three of DeltaGen’s founders are moving to Worker. DeltaGen’s team of around 10 people will stay in Prague.
Vilnius-based Biomatter , which uses AI to design enzymes, has raised an oversubscribed €16.2 million ($18 million) Series A . The round was led by Astanor , with existing investors UVC Partners, Inventure and Metaplanet also taking part. Founded in 2018, Biomatter designs enzymes by starting from the chemical reaction a customer needs .
Czech medtech startup Kardi AI has raised €5.3 million in a Series A round led by German healthtech fund Callisto Health. According to the company, this is the largest round a Czech medtech startup has raised to date. Česká spořitelna and Slovenská sporiteňa joined through their corporate venture programmes. Earlier backers BrightCap Ventures, Purple Ventures, DEPO Ventures and Garage Angels also put in money. After the round, Kardi AI is valued at €23 million.
Hedepy, the Prague-based online therapy platform operating in nine European countries, has secured €4 million in venture debt from Orbit Capital to fund acquisitions and expand into clinical care and AI tools — aiming to consolidate Europe’s fragmented mental health market.
Valkyrie Dynamics, the Ukrainian-Lithuanian defense startup building a 100-gram radar seeker that lets low-cost drones intercept targets through cloud and fog, raised €1 million in a pre-seed round led by Paris-based venture studio Hexa — developed and field-tested alongside operators in Kyiv.
Romanian edtech company Kinderpedia , which has developed a management and communication platform for schools and kindergartens, has secured a €500,000 investment from BCR Seed Starter , the corporate venture capital arm of BCR. The investment completes Kinderpedia’s €2.7 million funding round , led by Polish fund Simpact Ventures, with participation from existing investors Early Game Ventures and ROCA X.
